messages.content:
The issue seems to be related to handling long directory names when adding them to a TAR archive. The failing test is trying to add a directory with a name longer than 100 bytes, which leads to an exception when writing PAX headers. The stack trace indicates that there is an issue with writing more bytes than allowed for the entry header.

Looking at the `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveOutputStream` class, the `putArchiveEntry` method is responsible for adding entries to the TAR archive. This method performs checks and handles the entry based on various modes and configurations.

The key part related to the issue is the section that deals with long file names. If the file name exceeds the allowed length, different actions are taken based on the `longFileMode`. In the case of `LONGFILE_POSIX`, PAX headers with the full path are added. However, there is a condition that checks for non-ASCII characters and adds a PAX header for the path in that case. This behavior can lead to additional bytes being written to the header, causing the exception observed in the failing test.

To address this issue, we need to modify the logic in the `putArchiveEntry` method to handle long directory names properly, particularly when dealing with non-ASCII characters and adding PAX headers.

Next, I will provide the methods that should be fixed to resolve this issue.
`org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveOutputStream.putArchiveEntry(org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.ArchiveEntry)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
